Hi Ellen —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + three concrete asks so we can get a scoped quote over to procurement: 

Recap (what you shared)
- Primary workload: customer support automation + personalized summaries for care teams.
- Expected baseline monthly token consumption: ~75M tokens/month (see ask #1 below).
- Traffic profile: steady daytime usage (~120 TPS sustained) with campaign-driven spikes. You estimated short promotional blasts that could reach ~375–400 TPS for <10 minutes.
- Target $/1M tokens: you mentioned a target band in RFP of ~$475–650? (need confirmation).

Asks (to confirm)
1) Please confirm the expected average monthly tokens (conservative / expected / aggressive). E.g. conservative 40M | expected 75M | aggressive 150M — is that aligned?
2) Confirm peak TPS expectations: is 120 TPS sustained + bursts to 400 TPS reasonable? Any percent of requests that are low-latency vs batchable?
3) Budget band / target $/1M tokens you want us to aim for in the quote. If procurement gave a specific $/1M target or a target spend range, drop it here.

What I'll do next
- Attach a short workbook (token-scenarios.xlsx) showing per-scenario unit economics and a first-pass hosted vs dedicated recommendation.
- If you confirm the three items above, I’ll send a 1-page pricing scenarios PDF and a draft payer-friendly quote for procurement.

Deadline: if we can lock the scenarios by EOD Thu (May 31), I can get a procurement-friendly quote to you by Mon Jun 3.

Thanks — looking forward.

— Markus

Hi Markus —

Appreciate the recap. Confirming details from our side:
- Monthly tokens: our internal projection is "expected" ~75M tokens/month. For planning purposes we want to see two alternative scenarios as you suggested: conservative 45M / expected 75M / aggressive 160M.
- Peak TPS: core production steady-state ~120 TPS. Marketing/promotions (approx 3–4x/month) can spike to ~350–400 TPS for short windows (5–12 minutes). Roughly 8% of traffic is ultra-low-latency (sub-150ms critical). The rest can tolerate small batching delays.
- Budget target: procurement asked us to try to aim for a pricing envelope around $150–$220 per 1M tokens for committed volume; they wrote that in the RFP as a preferred goal but will accept higher if SLA/throughput guarantees require it.

Two small clarifications:
1) Are the burst/overflow autoscaling costs accounted for in hosted pricing (or do we need a dedicated burst pool)?
2) We will likely request SOC2 artifacts and an exec summary on data residency for the quote packet (procurement asked).

If you can send the scenarios workbook + a 1-page pricing scenarios PDF, procurement will review and come back with any legal redlines.

Thanks,

Ellen —

Thanks, this is exactly what we needed. I ran the numbers and attached a short pricing estimate (redwood-pricing-estimate.pdf) — high level summary below. Workbook has the per-scenario math and assumptions.

Pricing scenarios (hosted first-pass) — per 1M token unit economics and monthly totals for the three scenarios you confirmed:
- Conservative (45M/mo): $/1M = $225 -> est monthly cost $10,125
- Expected (75M/mo): $/1M = $175 -> est monthly cost $13,125
- Aggressive (160M/mo): $/1M = $140 -> est monthly cost $22,400

Notes on throughput and SLA handling
- Sustained 120 TPS is comfortably served by hosted pools; brief 350–400 TPS spikes are handled via burst autoscaling but will increase short-term token spend and may hit request queuing depending on concurrency.
- For your ultra-low-latency (8% of traffic) we recommend a small Dedicated pool or reserved slots on Hosted (hybrid) to avoid cold-starts and queuing at peaks. I flagged a dedicated-qual sketch in the workbook (additional monthly commit and burst credits).
- If procurement prioritizes lower $/1M, committed-reserved pricing and a 12–24 month capacity commitment unlocks the $140 band in the aggressive scenario.

Next steps I propose
1) I’ll put together a 1-page pricing scenarios PDF and a procurement-friendly quote (including SOC2 link and data residency language).
2) Marissa / Karthik, can you confirm whether we want to present a Dedicated + Hosted hybrid as the default recommendation for this account? If yes, I’ll include a short ops note with expected commit levels and burst model.
3) Ellen, if you can share a preferred procurement contact or a DocuSign owner, I’ll draft the first quote next week (target Mon Jun 3).

Attachments: redwood-pricing-estimate.pdf (1-page scenarios) and token-scenarios.xlsx.
